A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SpargeAttn study, with complete, readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A.1-A.3. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original generation-quality, attention-speed, and latency measurements. The appendix includes permutation and self-similarity ablations and additional retrieval results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical measurements in Section 4 and Appendix A, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and generated image/video examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same selective token compression, sparse masking, warp-level softmax filtering, SageAttention integration, hyperparameter selection, and HilbertCurve permutation procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same language, image, and video generation coverage using WikiText, LongBench, InfiniteBench En.MC, Needle-in-a-Haystack, Open-Sora prompts, and COCO annotations. The appendix's shorter-context retrieval scenario is also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Full-Attention, MInference, and FlexPrefill in the corresponding comparisons. Table 2's SageAttn comparison and Figure 9's attention configurations are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The models, sequence lengths, metrics, hyperparameter thresholds, and testing procedures are unchanged. Appendix A retains the five-prompt permutation study, query/key block sizes of 128/64, and the same case-selection criterion.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix A retain the same prediction-overhead, permutation, self-similarity-judge, mask-component, and sequence-length analyses. The qualitative comparison examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version adds seed information, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Appendix A.2 retains its existing selection rule based on an absolute L1-error difference exceeding 0.05.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted trends, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendix. For example, Table 2 retains Mochi's 1037-second SpargeAttn latency, and Table 11 retains 443.6 TOPS and 0.863 retrieval accuracy.

T1.justification: Definitions 1-2, the sparse FlashAttention equations, and the online-softmax derivation in Section 3 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or formal results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims of universal, training-free sparse and quantized attention that accelerates diverse generative models while preserving end-to-end quality.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations linking token locality to compression, sparse attention to relevant-information selection, and longer contexts to greater sparsity. The appendix's robustness interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged.

D1.justification: CUDA implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and appendix permutation instructions are unchanged. Both PDFs already provide the same code link and SageAttention2 implementation notice, including the additional 30% speedup statement; the reworded footnote adds no technical disclosure.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The SageAttention2 bibliography entry changes from a URL-based reference to an explicit arXiv-preprint citation for the same work.

P1.justification: v2 slightly rephrases the first-page implementation footnote, updates the arXiv version/date stamp, and reformats the SageAttention2 reference. The section structure and almost all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: In Appendix A.1, the captions for Tables 8 and 9 move from below to above their tables. There are also small first-page text-flow changes; the figures and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 retains the same method, empirical evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information, including the appendix. The footnote and bibliography edits and relocated captions for Tables 8-9 are cosmetic adjustments without a material effect on overall paper quality.
